description: Garlic Naan Tandoor Bread is a beloved Indian flatbread, soft and chewy with a delightful garlic aroma. Traditionally baked in a tandoor oven, this leavened bread is brushed with butter or ghee for a rich finish. It makes a perfect accompaniment to any curry or stew, adding a burst of flavor to your meal.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine warm milk, warm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: To the yeast mixture, add the plain yogurt, vegetable oil, and salt. Mix well. Gradually add the all-purpose flour, one cup at a time, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Incorporate the minced garlic into the dough.

instructions.title: Knead and Rise
instructions.text: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a clean cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Naan
instructions.text: Once risen, gently punch down the dough and divide it into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into an oval or teardrop shape, about 1/4 inch thick. You can sprinkle a little flour to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Cook the Naan
instructions.text: Preheat a cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until smoking. Optionally, preheat your oven to its highest setting with a pizza stone or baking steel. Place one naan bread onto the hot skillet. Cook for 1-2 minutes until bubbles form on the surface. Flip and cook the other side for another 1-2 minutes until lightly browned and cooked through. If using an oven, place the naan directly on the hot stone/steel and bake for 2-3 minutes until puffed and lightly charred.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: As each naan is cooked, brush generously with melted butter or ghee and sprinkle with fresh chopped cilantro. Stack them on a plate and cover with a clean kitchen towel to keep warm. Serve immediately with your favorite Indian curries or dishes.

tips: For the best texture, ensure your cooking surface (skillet or oven stone) is extremely hot before placing the naan. This mimics the high heat of a traditional tandoor.
Using full-fat yogurt in the dough contributes significantly to the naan's tenderness and rich flavor. Do not substitute with low-fat versions if possible.
Naan is best enjoyed fresh off the pan. If you must store leftovers, reheat them briefly in a dry skillet or microwave to restore some softness.
